input: root is a nonempty finite acyclic binary tree with exactly n distinct ordinary nodes, no shared child, and distinct values 1 through n. n is positive and odd; x is a present node value. Each node has val,left,right data fields, with absent children None/null. All collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections. Node fields, where present, are ordinary data fields. Every individual collection length and computed allocation dimension/count fits [0,4294967295]; explicitly stated padded sizes and heap child-index arithmetic must also fit the declared exact numeric domain. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is permitted. Preconditions are not runtime-checked; allocation/resource capacity and actual completion still require qualification. Python integer inputs are plain int excluding bool; any separately declared floating probabilities are ordinary float.
return: Boolean indicating whether the second player can choose a different initial node and force a strict majority in the binary-tree coloring game when the first player chose x.
mutation_aliasing: No node field, input identity or caller alias changes. Local identity-to-size map and stack remain private; the Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Subtree counts are in [0,n], and comparison doubles at most n; 2*n must be safe. Python id values are opaque identity keys; JavaScript Map keys use object identity. Removing x partitions the tree into left, right and parent-side components. All integer inputs and integer intermediates (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain in [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: Expected O(n + 1) time and O(n + 1) auxiliary space, counting the identity size map and O(h+1) explicit postorder stack. A winning move exists exactly when one component has more than half the nodes. Bounds count ordinary built-in allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop, and stated hash/sort guarantees where relevant.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 1030 UTF-8 bytes, including every helper definition, Solution wrapper, signatures, loops, built-in calls, comments/annotations, whitespace and terminal newline.
